deck.title: API Gateway
deck.analogy: API Gateway is the front desk of a busy office building: it routes visitors, checks ID, turns away crowds, and logs every visit before your code runs.

cards.front: What does API Gateway do before your backend code runs?

back.answer: It routes, authenticates, throttles, caches, and logs requests as a fully managed front door to your backend.
back.explanation: It sits in front of Lambda or other backends and handles routing, auth, rate limiting, caching and monitoring.
back.mnemonic: Front desk of an office building: routes, checks ID, turns away crowds, writes the logbook.

cards.front: What is the canonical serverless chain involving API Gateway?

back.answer: Client → CloudFront → API Gateway → Lambda → DynamoDB.
back.explanation: Reflex: "no servers to manage, pay per request" means this chain.
back.code: Client --> CloudFront --> API Gateway --> Lambda --> DynamoDB

cards.front: API Gateway REST API: personality, features, and trigger phrase?

back.answer: Full-featured flagship: API keys, usage plans, caching, WAF, request validation. Choose it when you need any of those.

cards.front: API Gateway HTTP API: personality, features, and trigger phrase?

back.answer: Minimalist, ~70% cheaper: simple proxy to Lambda/HTTP, built-in JWT auth, low latency. Trigger: "lowest cost".

cards.front: API Gateway WebSocket API: personality, features, and trigger phrase?

back.answer: Persistent two-way connection; server can push to clients. Trigger: real-time chat, live push, live dashboards.

cards.front: Trap: a question needs API Gateway usage plans, API keys, or caching. Is HTTP API a valid choice because it's cheaper?

back.answer: No. Usage plans, API keys, and caching are REST API only; HTTP API is a distractor.
back.explanation: HTTP API is cheaper but lacks these features.

cards.front: API Gateway Edge-Optimized endpoint: what is it for?

back.answer: Globally distributed clients; routed through CloudFront's edge network automatically (the default).

cards.front: API Gateway Regional endpoint: when is it used?

back.answer: For clients in the same region, or when you want to attach your own CloudFront distribution.

cards.front: API Gateway Private endpoint: what is it and how is it reached?

back.answer: VPC-only access, reached via an Interface VPC Endpoint; never touches the internet.

cards.front: API Gateway IAM / SigV4 authorizer: when to use it?

back.answer: Caller is AWS-native (internal services, EC2 roles, IAM users); requests signed with SigV4.

cards.front: API Gateway Cognito User Pool authorizer: when to use it?

back.answer: Callers are app users who sign in (mobile/web); Cognito issues a JWT the gateway validates with zero custom code.

cards.front: API Gateway Lambda Authorizer: when to use it and what does it return?

back.answer: Custom logic: third-party IdP or bespoke tokens. Your Lambda inspects the token and returns an IAM policy.

cards.front: What is API Gateway's default throttle limit and the error clients get when exceeding it?

back.answer: 10,000 requests/second per account per region; excess gets HTTP 429 Too Many Requests.
back.explanation: Clients receiving 429 means you're being throttled.

cards.front: What do API Gateway Usage Plans and API Keys provide, and which API type supports them?

back.answer: Per-customer request quotas and rate tiers; REST API only.
back.explanation: Trigger: a SaaS company sells API access in Basic/Pro tiers.

cards.front: What is API Gateway caching's default TTL and its purpose?

back.answer: Default TTL is 300 seconds; it reduces backend load and latency.
back.explanation: Use it when repeated requests keep hitting the backend.

cards.front: Trap: API Gateway's backend takes over 29 seconds. Can you raise the timeout?

back.answer: No. 29 seconds is a hard maximum; go asynchronous instead.
back.explanation: Lambda can run 15 minutes, but not behind API Gateway. Return 202 Accepted, hand work to SQS or Step Functions, and let the client poll or be notified.
back.code:
Client --> API GW --202--> (immediately)
              |
              +--> SQS --> Lambda/worker (takes 2 min, nobody's waiting)

cards.front: Browser JavaScript on one domain is blocked calling your API Gateway on another domain. What's the fix?
Build a REST API with no servers to manage, paying only per request. Which architecture?
A SaaS company wants different API request limits per pricing tier. What do you use in API Gateway?

back.answer: Usage Plans + API Keys (REST API only).

choices.why: No usage plans on HTTP API.

cards.front: Mobile app users must sign in before calling the API Gateway API. Which authorizer?

choices.why: Validates Cognito JWTs for app users.
Needless custom code for standard sign-in.

cards.front: A company has an existing custom/third-party token system for API Gateway auth. What fits?
Cheapest way to expose a simple Lambda function over HTTP with JWT auth?
Push live updates to a real-time dashboard or chat app via API Gateway. Which API type?

choices.why: Server can push over persistent connection.

cards.front: An API Gateway API must be accessible only from within the VPC, never the internet. Solution?
Backend takes 2 minutes and API Gateway requests keep timing out. Fix?

back.answer: Go async: return 202, queue to SQS/Step Functions.
back.explanation: 29s is a hard limit; you cannot raise it.

choices.text: Raise the API Gateway timeout to 5 minutes
Return 202 and queue work to SQS/Step Functions

cards.front: Browser JavaScript from another domain gets blocked calling your API Gateway API. Fix?
Clients suddenly receive HTTP 429 errors from API Gateway. What is happening and what helps?

back.answer: Throttling; raise the limit or add caching/usage plans.

choices.why: CORS errors appear in the browser, not 429.

choices.text: Throttling; raise limit or add caching
